key_insight: Open-weight LLM agents can perform much of the tedious longitudinal data-preparation work locally, reducing reliance on cloud services for sensitive research data.
engineering_relevance: This work shows a practical path for governance-restricted research groups to use consumer-grade hardware for AI-assisted code generation and data cleaning.
method: Built an open-source benchmark from six sweeps of a British cohort study with ground-truth cleaning scripts.
Defined 20 data-preparation tasks, including category harmonization and multi-wave merging, spanning 102 variables.
Automatically evaluated model-generated R code and the resulting output data against the curated targets.
evidence_signal: Across 20 tasks, top 31–35B open-weight models nearly saturated the benchmark, reaching up to 87.9% average task completion.
watch_item: Performance is strong but not perfect, so critical data workflows still need human review and validation before use in research pipelines.
paper_title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
